ATP Finals 2026: Shelton beats Jodar, needs favour from Zverev to reach semifinals
 If Arthur Fils fails to beat Alexander Zverev in straight sets in the other group match on Thursday, Shelton will qualify for the last-four stage.
 Updated : Nov 19, 2026 21:31 IST , TURIN - 2 MINS READ

 USA’s Ben Shelton finished the group stage at this year’s ATP Finals with two wins and one loss in Turin, Italy.
 | Photo Credit: AP
 USA’s Ben Shelton finished the group stage at this year’s ATP Finals with two wins and one loss in Turin, Italy.
 | Photo Credit: AP
 World number four Ben Shelton had to battle for ​over two hours before carving out ‌a 7-6(8), 7-5 win over Spaniard ​Rafael Jodar at the ⁠ATP Finals on Thursday to close in on a semifinal spot.
 The US Open ‌finalist must wait for the result of the other group ‌match later on Thursday between ‌world ⁠number one Alexander Zverev, who ⁠has already made the semifinals, and France’s Arthur Fils. If Fils fails to beat Zverev in straight sets, Shelton will qualify for the last-four stage.
 The American, a Paris Masters finalist earlier ​this month, looked ‌in trouble when he struggled with Jodar’s serve and did not muster a break point in the first ‌set.
 It was Jodar who looked ​more likely to break the deadlock before Shelton got the ⁠edge in a tightly contested tiebreak.
 2 out of 3 ain't bad 👌
The moment Shelton secured victory over Jodar at the #NittoATPFinals https://t.co/GOqErfkGww
— Tennis TV (@TennisTV) November 19, 2026 He earned an early break in the second ‌set and looked firmly in control until Jodar won three consecutive games to go 5-4 up.
 Shelton, however, stayed composed and won two long and brutal baseline rallies to break ‌back before delivering a near-perfect service game ​to seal his win.
 The 20-year-old Jodar, who has enjoyed a ⁠sensational debut year on the tour shooting ⁠up from the mid-100s to the top 10 in less ‌than 12 months, will end his debut ATP Finals appearance with three ​group losses.
 “It was really tough,” Shelton said in his on-court interview. “Rafa is a great player. So many weapons and such a great competitor as well. I knew it wasn’t going to be an easy match going in and I was happy to get through some tough moments in the first set, early, when I was down break points to get to the tie-break.
 “When I was in the tie-break, I felt confident. A tricky second set and being up a break and losing it. But I think I fought well and competed well. The 5-5 game was a dogfight and I am really happy to get that W.”
